We need to decide which march order to resolve. According to pendingDecision: type resolve-single-march, and actionGuidance lists two legalOrderRegions: the-shivering-sea (orderId 1 March -1) with unitIds [4] (our ship) and white-harbor (orderId 2 March +0) with unitIds [3] (our footman). So we need to choose one starting region? Actually pendingDecision likely refers to the currently being resolved march order; which one is being resolved now? The actionGuidance shows legalOrderRegions both, but pendingDecision may indicate which order is being resolved (maybe the first in some order). However schema's starting_region_id enum includes both "the-shivering-sea" and "white-harbor". So we can pick either.

We must decide best move.

Consider supply: Stark supply =1, meaning allowed armies sizes: per table: supply 1 permits armies sizes 3,2 (two armies)?? Actually table: 1: 3,2? Wait supply track: at 1, permitted army sizes: 3,2 (so one army up to 3, one up to 2). Each army is 2+ units. Stark currently has units: at castle-black: footman (id1) and knight (id2) form an army of 2 units (size 2). At white-harbor: footman id3 alone (size 1, not an army). At the-shivering-sea: ship id4 alone (size 1, not an army). Total armies = 1 (castle-black). That's within supply.

If we move the ship from the-shivering-sea to somewhere. Reachable destinations for ship from the-shivering-sea: only listed reachableRegions for that order: the-narrow-sea (type sea, castleLevel 0). No combat there (no enemy). Ship can move there, creating a fleet (size 1) still not an army. Supply fine.

If we move footman from white-harbor. Reachable: castle-black (land, no castle). karhold (land). moat-cailin (land with castleLevel 1 stronghold). widows-watch (land). winterfell (your own castle). Also maybe other but listed. Only moat-cailin has castleLevel 1, which would capture a stronghold gaining a castle area (counts as a castle area for victory). White harbor currently provides 1 castle area (its own castle). If we vacate white harbor without leaving power token, we lose that castle area. So we can either keep it (no move) or move footman to moat-cailin capturing a stronghold and gaining castle area (net gain perhaps 0 because lose white harbor but gain moat-cailin). White harbor has a castle (castle=2 stronghold) counted as a castle area. Moat-cailin is a stronghold (castleLevel 1) also counts as one area. So net same count. But also we could keep white harbor and maybe later move something else. Leaving power token costs 1 power token. Stark has 5 power tokens, could spend.

If we move footman to moat-cailin, need to consider support for potential combat? There is no enemy there currently (controller null). So no combat; we capture it, adding castle area. But we also lose white harbor's castle area. Net zero. However we also lose the garrison? White harbor had no garrison; just had our footman. Also we preserve supply fine.

If we move footman to castle-black, we would join our existing army (2 units) making 3 units (footman + footman + knight). That's still a single army of 3 units, allowed (max 3). No castle gained (castle-black has no castle). No castle lost if we leave power token? If we vacate white harbor, we lose that castle area unless we leave power token. We could leave power token (cost 1). Then we keep castle area while moving footman away, leaving white harbor empty but controlled via power token. That maintains castle count. That's likely best to keep the castle while moving footman to join forces.

We have to consider that we might want to attack something. Destinations: moat-cailin is adjacent to white harbor, but includes a castleLevel 1 (stronghold). Could attack if there were enemy but none. Also could be used for future attacks.

The ship move to the-narrow-sea is a sea area; no immediate benefit.

Given we have a March -1 order at the-shivering-sea, which gives -1 combat strength if combat triggered. But we probably not attack there.

Which March order to resolve? The pendingDecision may be processing each order sequentially; maybe we already resolved winterfell earlier? In history, previous action resolved winterfell moving units 1,2 to castle-black. That was earlier (action id 10). Now we have two remaining March orders: white-harbor (+0) and the-shivering-sea (-1). Now we need to resolve one of them. The schema allows choosing either.

We should pick the white-harbor +0 order to move footman to moat-cailin (capture stronghold) while leaving power token to keep white harbor. This would net +0 castle count but strengthen position and maybe future movement. Also we could consider moving to winterfell (our own) to consolidate, but need to keep control token for white harbor.

Option: leave_power_token = true, move unit 3 to winterfell (our own), keep castle area. That results in footman at winterfell (now 2 units there with footman & ship? Actually winterfell currently has no units, just castle and garrison. Moving footman there forms an army of 1 unit (size1), not an army, still ok. No combat. Keeping power token keeps white harbor castle. Net same castle count.

Which is better? Might want to concentrate forces at winterfell (home) for defense. Also white harbor is a coastal area near sea where we have ship in shivering sea; maybe keep presence there for naval control. If we move footman away, white harbor still empty but controlled by token; we still have ship later could move there. Retaining ship presence? Ship remains in the-shivering-sea if we don't move it. Could later move ship to white harbor via port? Actually white harbor is land, not a port. So ship cannot go there.

Probably best to keep footman at white harbor for defense (since ship in adjacent sea). So maybe we should not move footman now, but we must resolve the order; we could discard it (empty moves list) to remove the order; but then we lose ability to move later? Not needed. If we discard, we lose the ability to move that footman this turn, but we lose nothing else. Could also keep footman and leave power token false? That would vacate white harbor lose castle area. Not good.

Thus decision: resolve white-harbor order, leave unit there (i.e., empty moves list) to keep castle? But the order would be discarded and footman stays. That seems best: do not move footman, keep castle area. However note that leaving power token is false (cannot because unit remains). Moves empty -> order removed, no token needed. That's allowed. Then footman stays, castle area retained.

But there is also the other order (the-shivering-sea) still pending later. We'll need to resolve later. So choose starting_region_id "white-harbor", moves [], leave_power_token false.

However schema requires moves array, could be empty list. Yes allowed. Must meet constraints: each unit ID at most once; empty moves discards order. That's okay.

Thus final answer:

{
 "starting_region_id":"white-harbor",
 "moves":[],
 "leave_power_token":false
}

Check: enum for starting_region_id includes both. Moves array empty allowed? Schema says moves maxItems 1 but not minItems. So empty array acceptable. Provide.

Return JSON.

We need to decide order assignments for five regions: bay-of-ice, castle-black, karhold, winterfell, the-narrow-sea. Must follow constraints: maxStarredOrders=0 (from planningConstraints). So cannot assign starred orders (special orders). Must avoid raid category (restricted). So allowed categories: march, defense, support, consolidate_power. Also must assign exactly one order per region (since each occupied area requires an order). No starred tokens.

We need to consider strategic needs. Let's examine current units:

- bay-of-ice: contains a Stark ship (id 34). No land units. It's a sea area adjacent to castle-black (land), karhold (land), the-shivering-sea (sea), winterfell (land), the-narrow-sea (sea). Also has port-of-winterfell? Actually port-of-winterfell is a port area separate, not part of bay-of-ice; but bay-of-ice adjacent to port-of-winterfell? It's listed as neighbour. Okay.

- castle-black: land with 2 Stark knights.

- karhold: land with 1 Stark knight.

- winterfell: land with 1 Stark footman (plus garrison 2) and maybe a ship? Actually winterfell has footman only; but there is a ship in bay-of-ice adjacent. Also port-of-winterfell is adjacent.

- the-narrow-sea: sea with Stark ship (id 4). Adjacent to many sea areas: crackclaw-point, moat-cailin, port-of-white-harbor, shipbreaker-bay, the-eyrie, the-fingers, the-mountains-of-the-moon, the-shivering-sea, the-twins, white-harbor, widows-watch.

We need to consider supply: Stark supply is 1 (very low). Currently they have 1 army? Let's count armies: Any area with 2+ units is an army. At present: bay-of-ice (1 ship) alone -> not an army. castle-black (2 knights) -> that's an army (size 2). karhold (1 knight) -> single unit not army. winterfell (1 footman) -> single unit not army. the-narrow-sea (1 ship) -> not army. So only one army (castle-black) size 2. Supply 1 permits one army of size up to 1? Wait supply track: supply 1 allows army sizes 3 and 2? Actually table: Supply 0: army sizes 2,2. Supply 1: 3,2. So supply 1 allows one army up to size 3 and a second army up to size 2? Wait table: "Permitted army sizes". For supply level 1: 3,2. Means can have up to 2 armies; one of size up to 3, another up to 2. Currently we have one army size 2 => okay. Adding another army of size >=2 would create second army of size 2 (if you create two units in same area). That's allowed under supply 1 (since we can have a second army up to 2). So it's okay.

But must not exceed number of armies and sizes. If we march units out of castle-black we might leave it empty (0 units) If we don't place a Power token, we lose control; but castle is a castle, still controlled if we have a Power token? Actually control of castle area defined by units or control token. If we leave castle empty and no power token, we lose control. The strategic note earlier says preserve castles. So probably we want to keep defense on castle-black to hold it.

Similarly karhold is a castle (actually not castle? It's castle? In map: karhold has crown=1 but not castle? It says castle? Not in attributes, just crown. So not a castle but maybe a stronghold? Not indicated. It's just a land area, no castle. Not needed to defend.

Winterfell is a castle (home). Should defend.

The-narrow-sea is a sea area with no castle; could do consolidate power for power tokens (but per rules, consolidating power in open sea yields no power unless there are power icons on area; there are none. So consolidating power in sea yields nothing. However there is a ship there, could use March order to move ships maybe with support. Perhaps could march ship to bay-of-ice, etc. But we have also a ship in bay-of-ice. Since supply is low, we want to avoid creating extra armies > supply. Marching ship from the-narrow-sea to adjacent sea with enemy ships could cause combat, but there are none. Potentially march ship to the-shivering-sea? Adjacent? The-narrow-sea adjacent to the-shivering-sea, which is currently empty? Actually the-shivering-sea has no units listed. So could march ship there to reposition for ship transport later.

But maybe we want to use support orders to help somewhere else? Support can add combat strength to either side if combat occurs. Might be useful for future attacks.

We have limited star orders (0). So we may just assign orders accordingly.

We should prioritize defense on winterfell and castle-black to hold castles. On karhold maybe support (to aid any attack from castle-black). Bay-of-ice we can maybe assign march -1 or +0 or +1? We only have regular March orders: there are two regular March orders: one -1, one +0. Also one Special March +1 but we cannot use starred. Which one will we get? Preference is just category; the harness will allocate the actual token. We may want a March order (maybe +0) from bay-of-ice to try to march ship to winterfell? Actually ship cannot go to land directly; need port. We have port-of-winterfell adjacent to winterfell and bay-of-ice. The ship in bay-of-ice could move into port-of-winterfell (if we assign March order to bay-of-ice) and then later use transport to move knights? Actually ship transport only moves land units via ships, but ship itself cannot transport. So maybe we want the ship to stay for future transport.

Thus maybe assign Consolidate Power on bay-of-ice? But CP in sea gets no power, but could be okay. However maybe better to assign Support in bay-of-ice to support an attack from castle-black into north? Not sure.

We have limited supply; any new army creation must be okay.

Let's view neighbours to consider future moves:

- From castle-black knights could march to winterfell (adjacent via bay-of-ice? No direct; castle-black adjacent to bay-of-ice, karhold, the-shivering-sea, winterfell. So could march knights into winterfell (which already has footman) to create army of 2 units (size 2) at winterfell; that would vacate castle-black (lose it). Not good.

- Could march knights to karhold (occupied by own knight) combine into larger army; but that would exceed supply (two knights together -> army size 2). Still okay. But would leave castle-black empty.

Thus better to keep defense orders.

So propose assignments:

- winterfell: defense (to protect home castle). (priority high)

- castle-black: defense (to protect castle). (high)

- karhold: support (to possibly support castle-black attack elsewhere). (mid priority)

- bay-of-ice: support (maybe support any attack planned). Or could be march? But March will move ship away maybe not needed. Support order on sea cannot support land combat (only sea). So maybe better to assign march to use ship later. But we have no target now. Might be okay to assign consolidate power (but yields nothing). But may want to keep ship for future transport; leaving it idle is fine.

We have 5 orders required. We must assign a category to each region. Use categories: defense, support, consolidate_power, march.

Given we have no starred orders, we can assign any of those.

I think:

- winterfell: defense (priority 100)

- castle-black: defense (priority 90)

- karhold: support (priority 80)

- bay-of-ice: support (priority 70) (since ship can provide support in sea combat if combat arises adjacent; but support on sea can support combat in sea area only, not land.)

- the-narrow-sea: consolidate_power (priority 60) maybe to gain power? Actually it's empty of power icons so CP yields 1 power token (the token from order itself) but no icons. Wait Consolidate Power order gives one Power token plus icons. So CP in sea with no power icons still gives 1 power token. Yes rule: Consolidate Power order gives one power token from the pool, plus additional for each power icon. So we can get 1 power token from the-narrow-sea. That seems useful.

Thus assign Consolidate Power to the-narrow-sea.

Ensure not exceeding starred limit (none). No raid orders.

All good.

Now construct JSON.

Check orderLegend mapping: order IDs for categories (but not needed). We'll just specify preferences; harness creates actual orders.

Thus final JSON with assignments list.

actionOutputSchema.description: You are placing planning orders for this round. We need to decide how to move units from Winterfell (region id winterfell) based on March +0 order. ActionGuidance shows reachableRegions list with possible destinations and for each, supplySafeUnitIdGroupsWhenChosenAlone: [[45]] meaning unit id 45 (the lone knight) can move alone safely supply-wise. We can also split? Only one group allowed? Moves array maxItems 1, so only one destination group? Actually schema: moves is array of up to 1 item (maxItems 1). Each item has only destination_region_id, no unit list. So must move all units? The description says moves list groups, but schema limited to one group; maybe each move object includes only destination_region_id, and it's implied that all units from source move? But we can only move one group due to maxItems 1. Probably they designed to move all units or none.

Thus we must choose a destination region id among list. We need to consider capture of castles and potential combat. Options:

- castle-black (land, no castle, no combat). Would just move to own controlled area (Stark already controls). No castle gain.

- flints-finger (land, castleLevel 1, currently controlled by Greyjoy. No combat (triggersCombat false). Means if you move into a territory with enemy units? But there are no units there currently. So you capture castle without combat. Gains castle point.

- greywater-watch (land, no castle, triggersCombat true (enemy units present). Greywater-watch has Greyjoy units (footman, 2 knights). So moving there would initiate combat.

- karhold (land, own area, no combat.

- moat-cailin (land, castleLevel 1, controlled by Greyjoy. No combat.

- the-stony-shore (land, no controller, no castle.

- white-harbor (land, castleLevel 1, no controller.

We cannot place control token because canLeavePowerToken false, but it says "Winterfell currently contributes 1 castle area to your score. Your existing control token or home symbol keeps this area yours when you leave it empty; no new token is needed." So we can vacate Winterfell without token.

Supply track: Stark supply = 1. Means allowed army sizes: from supply table, supply 1 gives army sizes 3,2? Actually table: supply 1 => permitted army sizes 3,2. So can have up to two armies: one up to 3 units, another up to 2 units.

Currently after mustering we have: Winterfell: one knight (id45). Castle Black: two knights (ids2,28). Karhold: one knight (id29). The Narrow Sea: one ship (id4). So units: knights (total 4) and ship (1). Armies: castle black has 2 knights (army size 2). karhold has 1 knight (single unit not army). winterfell has 1 knight (single). narrow sea has 1 ship (single). So currently there are no armies (needs >=2 units). Supply limit is fine.

If we move the knight from winterfell to a destination, we will vacate winterfell (no units). Since we have no control token needed, winterfell remains under Stark control (home area) automatically.

After moving, we will have still knights elsewhere. No new army unless we move into area with existing Stark unit to create army (but we only have one unit moving). So supply safe.

Goal: capture a castle without combat, to increase victory points. Options: Flints Finger (castle), Moat Cailin (castle), White Harbor (castle). Also maybe The Stony Shore no castle. Among these, which are reachable? Yes all in list.

We should consider support around potential destination battle if we choose combat at Greywater-watch. But that would involve combat against Greyjoy's troops, risky.

Better to capture a castle without combat, gaining victory point. Choose whichever is strategically valuable: Flints Finger is in the north, near Greyjoy holdings and gives access to sea. Moat Cailin is also castle, but currently controlled by Greyjoy, located near The Twins, etc. White Harbor also castle, near the Neck.

Which is more valuable? Iron throne track? Need to consider future moves. Perhaps capturing Flints Finger is good to expand into the North, but it's isolated. Moat Cailin would give control of a strategic choke point (The Twins). White Harbor gives control over another northern seaboard.

We must ensure we can move there via valid adjacency (Winterfell adjacency list includes flints-finger, moat-cailin, white-harbor, castle-black, karhold, the-stony-shore). So all reachable.

We should also consider that moving to Flints Finger might allow ship transport later (but currently we have a ship in The Narrow Sea). Flints Finger is land; no port.

White Harbor also land.

Moat Cailin is also land.

Which gives more support potential for future? Also maybe there is a ship in The Narrow Sea that could support later.

Probably capture Moat Cailin because it's near The Twins, controlling the passage. But also Flints Finger is a castle area controlled by Greyjoy; taking it would reduce Greyjoy's castle count from 4 to 3, improving relative standing. Moat Cailin also reduces Greyjoy's castles.

Which is more contested? Greyjoy also holds Flints Finger (castle) and Moat Cailin (castle) and White Harbor. All three are Greyjoy castles.

Maybe choose one where there is less immediate support needed to hold? All are isolated; could be attacked later.

Given no immediate combat, any is fine. I think choose Flints Finger (castle) as simplest.

Thus move unit id45 (knight) from Winterfell to Flints Finger.

Make moves array with one object: destination_region_id "flints-finger". No need to specify unit ids (schema doesn't include). So moves: [{ "destination_region_id": "flints-finger"}].

- Also bay-of-ice can move to sunset-sea (sea) which has controller Greyjoy, triggers combat (since enemy ship present? Actually sunset-sea currently has one Greyjoy ship (id44) per board. Now consider moat-cailin.

From moat-cailin reachable: greywater-watch (land, no castle), seagard (land, castleLevel=2 stronghold), the-twins (land), white-harbor (land castleLevel=1), winterfell (castleLevel=2, already Stark). We need to assign orders for the four occupied areas: pyke, ironmans-bay, port-of-pyke, greywater-watch. We have 0 starred orders allowed (maxStarredOrders:0). So starred_preference must be avoid, and we cannot request starred orders. Also need to respect order categories may be any of march, defense, support, consolidate_power, raid. Need to consider strategy.

Current board: Greyjoy controls pyke (castle stronghold), ironmans-bay (sea with ship), port-of-pyke (port with ship), greywater-watch (land with footman). Supply is 2. Units: pyke has footman and knight. ironmans-bay has ship. port-of-pyke has ship. greywater-watch has footman. Supply icons controlled: pyke (castle stronghold=2 supply?) Actually pyke has castle=2 stronghold, supply=1. Greywater-watch supply=1. So supply icons =2 total. Supply track 2 gives permitted armies: from table supply 2 -> allowed army sizes 3,2,2. Currently Greyjoy has units: pyke (2 units = army size 2), ironmans-bay (1 ship alone not an army), port-of-pyke (ship alone not an army), greywater-watch (1 footman alone not an army). So only one army of size 2, within supply.

We need to decide orders. Goal: expand towards Flint's Finger (castle) reachable from pyke (land connection? Pyke neighbors: ironmans-bay, port-of-pyke. Ironmans-bay neighbors? it's sea, connects to pyke, port-of-pyke, flints-finger (land), greywater-watch (land?), actually check map: ironmans-bay list includes flints-finger, greywater-watch, etc. So from ironmans-bay (sea) we can march ship to flints-finger (castle) if adjacent? Ironmans-bay adjacent to flints-finger (land). Yes. So could assign a March order at ironmans-bay to move ship into flints-finger to attempt capture. That would be a March order, likely with +0 or +1? We have two normal March orders: one -1, one +0, and one special March +1 but cannot use starred (special). So we can assign March order (choose which modifier?). The orderLegend shows March -1 is id 1, March +0 id 2, March +1 special id 3. So normal March orders are -1 and +0. For attacking a castle with ship, we need combat strength. Ship unit has strength 1, plus March order modifier could be -1 or 0. Since enemy likely has no units there (undefended castle) the combat is just us moving into empty castle area. No combat needed? Actually moving into an empty area with a castle: you must have a March order to move; since there are no enemy units, you just occupy it, no combat, and you claim control. So March -1 or +0 fine. Preference maybe March +0 for better chance if opposition may contest later. But no combat now. So assign March order at ironmans-bay.

For port-of-pyke: you have a ship at port; you could assign a Support order perhaps to support future attacks. Or Raid to try to disrupt opponents. What are adjacent enemy orders? Need to check neighbours of port-of-pyke: neighbors are pyke and ironmans-bay. Both friendly. So no raid target. So Raid would be wasted. Support can be used later to support attacks from adjacent areas (pyke maybe). But to support you need a Support order in a region adjacent to combat. Port-of-pyke is adjacent to pyke (land) and ironmans-bay (sea). Could support attacks from pyke into ironmans-bay? Not needed. Maybe better to assign Defense to protect pyke? But pyke holds stronghold; defense order gives +1 on defense. That's useful. Could assign Defense at pyke.

Greywater-watch: footman there, adjacent to flints-finger (castle), moat-cailin (castle), seagard (castle). All undefended castles. Could assign March from greywater-watch to attack one of those. However we have only one March order left (since we used one at ironmans-bay), we have two normal March orders total. So we could use the other March -1 at greywater-watch to try capture flints-finger or seagard. But note that from greywater-watch, moving footman to flints-finger (adjacent land) will be March. That would leave greywater-watch empty; we may need to place a power token to retain control of that area (which has a supply icon and maybe a castle? Actually greywater-watch has supply=1 but no castle. No castle; leaving would lose a supply icon but we may not care? We have supply 2 already; losing supply token reduces supply icons controlled to 1, which might lower supply track? The Supply track depends on count of supply icons you control. You currently control 2 supply icons (pyke and greywater-watch). If you leave greywater-watch, you'll control only pyke (1). Then supply track may drop to 1 (lower). This would affect armies limit. Might be okay if we don't have many armies. But losing a supply icon reduces future mustering ability. Maybe better to keep a unit in greywater-watch and not march it away. Could assign Defense there to hold.

Then we would have March at ironmans-bay, Defense at pyke, Defense at greywater-watch, Consolidate Power at port-of-pyke? Consolidate power in a port yields no power but token. Could use Consolidate Power to perhaps muster? Special Consolidate Power no, but we have regular Consolidate Power order. Using it at port does nothing, wasted. Could use Raid? No adjacent enemy. Support? Could assign Support at port-of-pyke to support attacks from ironmans-bay perhaps. That would give +1 support maybe valuable later. Since no starred orders, we can assign support normal.

So final assignments:
- pyke: defense (avoid starred) priority high maybe 80.
- greywater-watch: support (or defense). Choose support to help future attacks from pyke/ironmans-bay? Support from greywater-watch could support attacks on adjacent combat like flints-finger later. Might be useful. Choose support.
- ironmans-bay: march (prefer +0) to move ship to Flint's Finger. But order token type: March +0 (id2). So preferred_order "march". priority high.
- port-of-pyke: support (or could be consolidate power but worthless). Choose support to have extra support. Or raid wasted. Use support.

We need to assign priority numbers from 0-100. Provide relative importance. Let's assign ironmans-bay priority 90, pyke 80, greywater-watch 70, port-of-pyke 60.

All starred_preference avoid. Provide JSON.

actionOutputSchema.title: submit_orders_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are placing planning orders for this round. Assign an order preference to each required occupied area, respecting the displayed restrictions and starred-order limit. Your final answer submits the whole order draft and marks your house ready. These orders determine what your armies can do later; this decision does not move units. A single land unit can capture an empty castle with a March order. Defence and Support orders do not move that unit or claim neighbouring land. Consolidate Power in an open sea earns no power; a port follows the separate port rule. The harness allocates the physical order tokens, preserving higher-priority preferences when not all requested categories fit the available tokens.

content.text:
We need to select 2 distinct unit IDs from possible [7,8,9,6,37]. We must consider strategy: which units to lose? Units are: 7 and 8 are ships in Port of Pyke (both Greyjoy ships). 9 is footman in Greywater Watch. 6 and 37 are knights in Greywater Watch.

We want to preserve strongest units and control. Considering supply and castle control: Greyjoy currently has supply 3, controlling 4 castle/stronghold areas. Units: at Port of Pyke (ships) likely important for transport and maybe future moves. Knights are strong units for combat. Footman is weaker.

Goal: preserve combat strength and ability to expand, also maintain supply. Losing ships may reduce transport ability but maybe okay. Knights are valuable for attacks. However, losing a knight could reduce ability to attack but still have one knight.

We must lose exactly two units. Probably lose the footman (9) and one ship (maybe 7) to preserve knights. Or lose both ships and keep knights and footman. Ships may be less crucial currently; knights are key for attacks. Since we have 2 knights, losing a ship is fine. Also losing footman may reduce numbers but we have enough supply anyway.

Thus choose unit IDs 7 (ship) and 9 (footman). That's two distinct.

Check if any rule about same region? pendingDecision says selectedUnitsMustBeOfSameRegion: false, so any region fine.

Thus final JSON: {"unit_ids_to_destroy":[7,9]}.
